note: Gaelic Dál Riata merged into broader Picto-Gaelic kingdom of Alba in ninth century; exact chronology debated.

_quarry.structural_significance: The Dál Riata-Pictish fusion under Kenneth MacAlpin (c. 843) synthesised Irish Gaelic and indigenous Pictish cultures into a distinctively Scottish identity; the adoption of Gaelic as the language of the new kingdom and the transfer of Columba's relics to Scone established the cultural and religious foundations of Scottish national identity.
